articles.title: COMMERCIAL USE OF PERSONAL ACCOUNTS
body: Use permissions: GitHub's Terms of Service explicitly allow a free personal account to be used for commercial projects. There is no penalty or mandatory fee for operating a commercial site or private repository under this model.

Ownership and independence: the project and source code are hosted under the client's account. If the project later needs to scale to a corporate setup, the account or repository can be migrated to a GitHub Organization without any service interruption.

articles.title: GITHUB PAGES HOSTING: CONDITIONS
body: GitHub Pages is a service designed to serve static web pages (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images). Its use for commercial websites is subject to the following guidelines:
list: Accepted sites: informational corporate sites, professional portfolios, landing pages, digital catalogs and brand blogs.

Commercial restrictions (prohibited use): GitHub Pages is not designed to function as a massive e-commerce platform (with complex transactional payment gateways managed on the same server), nor to resell hosting services or host applications as software-as-a-service (SaaS).

articles.title: TECHNICAL LIMITS OF FREE SERVICE
body: GitHub's free plan includes the following maximum limits per repository and published site:
list: Bandwidth (traffic): 100 GB per month — enough for thousands of monthly visits on an optimized site.
Published site size: maximum 1 GB — this applies to the files deployed for your website.
Repository size: maximum 1 GB (recommended) — the limit for source code stored on GitHub.
Compilations (builds): maximum 10 deployments per hour — applies when publishing or updating site content.
CI/CD minutes (Actions): 2,000 minutes per month — allocated for automating updates or running tests.
articles.note: Note on limits: if a site repeatedly exceeds the bandwidth limit (100 GB/month) or storage, GitHub won't suddenly charge you, but it may temporarily suspend the GitHub Pages service or send a notification asking you to optimize your content or migrate to a dedicated server.

articles.title: RESPONSIBILITIES AND RECOMMENDATIONS
body: To keep your published site running smoothly, we recommend the following:
list: Custom domain: for a proper commercial profile, we recommend linking a custom domain (for example: www.yourbusiness.com). DNS records and SSL certificate issuance cost nothing extra on GitHub.

Content backup: very high-resolution images or large files (such as videos or bulky PDFs) should be hosted on external storage services (such as Google Drive, AWS S3, or Cloudinary) so they don't exceed GitHub Pages limits.
Loss or modification of access: the Client is solely responsible for keeping their GitHub account and credentials secure, including email access and two-factor authentication (2FA).
